html:
SMTO-WEB-0035 — The answer's links to its research were mixed up

GUID: 21f0c24b-49c7-52cf-b31a-be4da45b325b
Slug: research-completion-claim-map-invalid
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • The Model labelled its statements in a way SMTO couldn't follow: a label was broken, repeated, or didn't match one place in the answer. The research itself is still saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to fix how it labels its statements. The Model usually corrects broken or repeated labels on another pass.
  2. If the run stops, ask a narrower question, for example about fewer items at a time. Long answers with many statements are more likely to exceed the label limits.
  3. If it keeps happening, ask the person who manages SMTO to choose a more capable Model in Settings › Setup (model routing). Getting these labels exactly right is a formatting step that some smaller Models struggle with.
  4. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. This publishes the answer without checking it against the research.

What success looks like

  • The answer appears with each statement followed by its source links.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with which Model the conversation used. Don't accept an answer whose labels point to text that isn't in the final answer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected the completion because the claim map is invalid: it fails CLAIM_SCHEMA, exceeds the message or claim-count limits, repeats claim IDs, or a claim's [[claim_id]] marker or text does not occur exactly once in the answer.

What this means

  • The claim map violates its schema, size or uniqueness limits, or each claim cannot locate exactly one marker or text span in the answer. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • The claim map violates its schema, size or uniqueness limits, or each claim cannot locate exactly one marker or text span in the answer.

How to diagnose it

  • Check message length, claim schema, unique IDs and exact marker occurrence counts.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_completion_claim_map_invalid in _validate_answer: message not a string or over 24000 characters, schema violations, more claims than research.limits.claims, duplicate claim_id, or a locator that appears zero or multiple times in the remaining uncovered text. Correct the claims array and use unique [[claim_id]] markers placed once in the message; map only text that exists in the final answer.
  • Correct the claim map and unique answer markers using existing evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • Each valid claim maps once to its displayed statement within the supported limits.

What not to do

  • Do not map evidence to text that is absent from or differs from the actual final answer.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
